chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them, has been transmitted by me from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them both - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Abu Al-Jawza' Al-Munabbih ibn Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عُلْوَانَ: Al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.زَيْدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Zayd ibn Ali, a prominent figure from the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator in Shia hadith
key_terms.عَمْرُو بْنُ خَالِدٍ: 'Amr ibn Khalid, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: What is the chain of transmission for narrations from Zayd ibn Ali in this book?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq employs this meta-narrative to authenticate the specific isnad of Zayd ibn Ali’s traditions, tracing the lineage through prominent Kufan scholars like al-Mufaddal ibn Umar and al-Husayn ibn Alwan to ensure the reliability of the Imamate's teachings. This explicit verification underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on rigorous chain-of-transmission analysis (ilm al-rijal) to preserve the integrity of hadiths from the Ahl al-Bayt.
